items.title: Show HN: ColliePWA, a self-hosted mobile terminal for coding agents, with alerts
items.contentSnippet:
Sharing the PWA[1] I built over the last couple of weeks to access my terminal sessions/agents when not in front of my computer. This started off as a weekend experiment right when herdr[2] (terminal multiplexer) released the functionality to write custom plugins and it's been quite helpful to me ever since. The general idea is that this runs a web app on the host machine which is then exposed through a front door implementation like tailscale/netbird/cloudflare tunnels etc.
A lot of devs/teams

items.title: Show HN: Airmash – HTML5 Multiplayer Missile Warfare
items.contentSnippet:
This is the official reboot of the 2017 hit game.
Back then it was #1 post on HN for 3 consecutive days: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=15892066
The game was rewritten from the ground up: New graphics, WebGL shader effects, Map obstacles, Completely new UI, Additional special ability for all aircraft, Daily/Weekly/Lifetime achievements, Levelling rewards, Loadout system for equipping skins, flags, flairs and titles, 5 game modes: FFA, CTF, Battle Royale, Racing, Zombies, Public leaderboard

items.title: Show HN: A poetry site for developers – solve a code puzzle to post
items.contentSnippet:
My passion or depression project.
A few days ago posted a short poem in my work chat about what AI is doing to our jobs as developers. A colleague replied with a poem of his own. Decided to check if this domain was free, and about €10 later, here is the site.
Anyone can post, but first you have to answer a one line "what does this print?" JS snippet.
No accounts, no emails, no tracking.
Since the poems are about AI, it seemed only fair to let AI post too.
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.c

items.title: Show HN: WTF > Auto-check what your coding agent changed
items.contentSnippet:
wTF is my attempt to understand all the development that my agents are doing all the time without getting splitting headaches and standing a chance of reading a couple of pages in any given book by the end of day. It gives me an overview of what actually happened.
It's also in early experimentation to see if it can help ground the agents in actual reality. Not there yet, though.
Free, open source, no API, 100% local.
